final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is meaningful analytically, but it is not enough to reach compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a disclosure note already proven complete. The admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and reversible phased rollout, but it also shows the legal intake triage weakness remains exposed and that rollout controls alone do not remove the disclosure duty. Without admissible proof of completed pre-launch disclosure, exclusion of the affected use case, or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, certification remains under-supported.
remaining_concerns: The affected legal intake triage segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The record still contains no approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses that exposed segment; the only related item is an unsigned draft that omits the exposure.
The governing policy and provided policy text both indicate that 5% rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy the predicate while the affected use case remains exposed.
There is still no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation was actually completed in launch materials or the model card.
